sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: WITH WEAK FLOW ALOFT/RIDGING TO GENERALLY PREVAIL ACROSS THE SRN CONUS...BELT OF FASTER FLOW ALOFT WILL REMAIN ACROSS THE NRN TIER OF THE COUNTRY...WITH A TROUGH EXPECTED TO CROSS THE NERN U.S. THROUGH THE PERIOD. AT THE SURFACE...A COLD FRONT WILL MOVE EWD ACROSS NEW ENGLAND AND SEWD ACROSS THE MID SOUTH REGION...WHILE A SECOND FRONT IS PROGGED TO CROSS THE NRN PLAINS. BOTH OF THESE BOUNDARIES SHOULD SUPPORT CONVECTION...WITH THE NRN PLAINS FRONT PROGGED TO BE THE FOCUS FOR THE PRIMARY SEVERE CONVECTIVE THREAT THIS PERIOD.

sections.title: NRN PLAINS REGION
sections.text: EARLY-PERIOD RIDGING ALOFT WILL MAINTAIN CAPPED AIRMASS INTO THE AFTERNOON ACROSS THE N CENTRAL CONUS...BUT AN APPROACHING COLD FRONT SHOULD PROVIDE SUSTAINED UVV SUFFICIENT TO WEAKEN THE CAP AND ALLOW SCATTERED STORM DEVELOPMENT...AS AFTERNOON HEATING LEADS TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF 2000 TO 3000 J/KG MIXED-LAYER CAPE ACROSS PORTIONS OF THE DAKOTAS. WHILE LOW-LEVEL FLOW SHOULD REMAIN FAIRLY WEAK...40 KT MID-LEVEL WLYS SPREADING ACROSS THIS REGION WILL SUPPORT ORGANIZED/ROTATING STORMS. THIS COMBINED WITH THE DEGREE OF INSTABILITY SUGGESTS POTENTIAL FOR LARGE HAIL...WHILE UPSCALE GROWTH INTO A MORE LINEAR MCS BY EVENING SUGGESTS THAT DAMAGING WINDS WILL ALSO BE A THREAT. LESS WIDESPREAD STORMS -- BUT WITH SOME HAIL/WIND POTENTIAL -- ARE ALSO FORECAST TO DEVELOP WWD INTO WY/SRN MT/ERN ID DURING THE AFTERNOON...BUT COMBINATION OF WEAKER FLOW ALOFT AND A LESS UNSTABLE AIRMASS SUGGEST MAINTAINING ONLY LOW SEVERE PROBABILITIES ATTM. ...OH/TN/MID AND LOWER MS VALLEYS INTO THE SOUTHEAST AND MID ATLANTIC... A LARGE AREA OF LOW PROBABILITY SEVERE POTENTIAL IS FORECAST TODAY...AS WIDESPREAD CONVECTION DEVELOPS IN RESPONSE TO LARGE-SCALE UPPER TROUGHING AND A WEAK SURFACE COOL FRONT BOTH PROGGED T

sections.title: AZ
sections.text: AFTERNOON STORM DEVELOPMENT IS AGAIN FORECAST ACROSS PORTIONS OF AZ AS AIRMASS HEATS/DESTABILIZES...THOUGH SOMEWHAT ISOLATED COVERAGE IS EXPECTED GIVEN LACK OF ANY APPARENT UPPER FEATURES. INITIAL STORMS SHOULD INITIATE OVER THE HIGHER TERRAIN IN SERN AZ...AS WELL AS INVOF THE MOGOLLON RIM. WITH ELY FLOW ALOFT...EXPECT STORMS DEVELOPING OVER THE SERN MOUNTAINS TO MOVE WWD OFF THE HIGHER TERRAIN INTO THE LOWER DESERTS...AND A FEW OF THE STRONGER STORMS MAY PRODUCE ISOLATED DAMAGING GUSTS. CONVECTION SPREADING WWD INTO THE EVENING SHOULD WEAKEN AFTER SUNSET.

sections.title: ME
sections.text: DESTABILIZING AIRMASS AHEAD OF AN ADVANCING COLD FRONT SHOULD LEAD TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF ISOLATED THUNDERSTORMS DURING THE AFTERNOON -- AS LARGE-SCALE TROUGH SHIFTS ACROSS ERN CANADA AND THE NERN CONUS. WHILE NEITHER THE FLOW FIELD ALOFT NOR THE DEGREE OF INSTABILITY ARE FORECAST TO BE EXCESSIVE...AMPLE AMOUNTS OF BOTH SUGGEST AT LEAST ISOLATED SEVERE THREAT WITH STRONGER STORMS. WILL THUS UPGRADE TO 5% PROBABILITY ACROSS THIS REGION...WITH A FURTHER UPGRADE TO SLIGHT RISK POSSIBLE ACROSS PARTS OF THE AREA IN LATER FORECASTS. ..GOSS/SMITH.. 07/04/2011

sections.title: NRN PLAINS THROUGH TONIGHT
sections.text: A MIDLEVEL SHORTWAVE TROUGH OVER NRN MT/SASKATCHEWAN WILL MOVE EWD AND CREST THE LARGE SCALE RIDGE...WHILE SMALLER SCALE EMBEDDED SPEED MAXIMA PROGRESS EWD OVER THE DAKOTAS/MN...AND NEWD FROM UT TO WY. AT THE SURFACE...A COLD FRONT WILL MOVE EWD/SEWD ACROSS ERN WY/THE DAKOTAS/NW MN THROUGH EARLY TONIGHT. AHEAD OF THE FRONT...LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE ADVECTION FROM THE S AND ANOTHER DAY OF EVAPOTRANSPIRATION WILL INCREASE BOUNDARY LAYER DEWPOINTS INTO THE LOWER 70S. THIS WILL COMBINE WITH DAYTIME HEATING BENEATH 7-8 C/KM MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES TO RESULT IN AFTERNOON MLCAPE VALUES OF 2500-4000 J/KG IN THE WARM SECTOR. AN INITIAL CLUSTER OF STORMS IS EXPECTED TO WEAKEN THIS MORNING OVER EXTREME NE ND...FOLLOWED BY A LULL IN CONVECTION UNTIL MID AFTERNOON WHEN NEW STORMS ARE EXPECTED ALONG THE COLD FRONT. THIS AFTERNOON CONVECTION IS EXPECTED TO BACK-BUILD SWD/SWWD ALONG THE FRONT FROM NE ND/NW MN TO CENTRAL AND ERN SD BY LATE AFTERNOON/EVENING. EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR OF 30-40 KT WILL BE SUFFICIENT FOR ORGANIZED STORM CLUSTERS AND A FEW EMBEDDED SUPERCELLS...SOME OF WHICH COULD PRODUCE VERY LARGE HAIL GIVEN THE LARGE CAPE AND STEEP LAPSE RATES. DAMAGING WINDS CAN ALSO BE EXPECTED...ESPECIALLY AS

sections.title: ERN TN/SE KY TO VA/NC THROUGH LATE EVENING
sections.text: A MIDLEVEL TROUGH AXIS JUST NW OF THE OH RIVER...WITH EMBEDDED AND CONVECTIVELY ENHANCED SPEED MAXIMA...WILL PROGRESS ESEWD TO KY/WV/VA BY EARLY TONIGHT. AN ACCOMPANYING WEAK SURFACE COLD FRONT WILL SAG SEWD INTO TN/NW NC/VA BY LATE AFTERNOON... PROVIDING A FOCUS FOR THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT...ALONG WITH OUTFLOW BOUNDARIES FROM ONGOING STORMS IN KY/TN. A SLIGHT ENHANCEMENT TO THE DEEP-LAYER SHEAR NEAR THE FRONT...IN COMBINATION WITH AFTERNOON MLCAPE OF 2000-3000 J/KG...WILL SUPPORT ORGANIZED MULTICELL CLUSTERS CAPABLE OF PRODUCING DAMAGING WINDS AND MARGINALLY SEVERE HAIL...MAINLY THIS AFTERNOON/EVENING.

sections.title: MAINE/NH THIS AFTERNOON
sections.text: A MIDLEVEL TROUGH OVER QUEBEC WILL MOVE EWD OVER MAINE THIS AFTERNOON...AS AN ASSOCIATED/WEAK COLD FRONT MOVES SLOWLY SEWD. SURFACE HEATING IN CLOUD BREAKS...AND MID-UPPER 60S BOUNDARY LAYER DEWPOINTS WILL SUPPORT A NARROW CORRIDOR OF MODERATE INSTABILITY /MLCAPE NEAR 1500 J PER KG/ ALONG THE FRONT THIS AFTERNOON WHEN SCATTERED THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT IS EXPECTED. GIVEN THE MODERATE INSTABILITY AND EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR OF 30-40 KT...A FEW STORMS WILL BE CAPABLE OF PRODUCING DAMAGING GUSTS AND LARGE HAIL BEFORE THE FRONT MOVES EWD AND INSTABILITY DIMINISHES THIS EVENING.

sections.title: CENTRAL/SRN AZ THIS AFTERNOON/EVENING
sections.text: BOUNDARY LAYER DEWPOINTS HAVE INCREASED INTO THE 60S FROM S OF THE RIM TO THE LOWER CO RIVER VALLEY...WITH PW VALUES AOA 2 INCHES OVER SW AZ. THIS MOISTENING AND CONVECTION YESTERDAY/OVERNIGHT HAVE REDUCED LAPSE RATES AND RESULTED IN AN ENVIRONMENT LESS CONDUCIVE TO HYBRID MICROBURSTS. STILL...WITH MODERATE INSTABILITY EXPECTED OVER THE LOWER DESERTS AND A CONTINUATION OF ELY/ESELY MIDLEVEL FLOW NEAR AND S OF THE RIM...A FEW STORMS COULD MOVE OVER THE LOWER DESERTS WITH THE POTENTIAL FOR STRONG DOWNBURSTS WINDS THIS AFTERNOON THROUGH LATE EVENING. ..THOMPSON/LEITMAN.. 07/04/2011

sections.title: THERE IS A SLGT RISK OF SVR TSTMS ACROSS PARTS OF ME/NH
sections.text: ...THERE IS A SLGT RISK OF SVR TSTMS FROM KY/TN INTO THE MID ATLANTIC STATES...

sections.title: NORTHERN PLAINS
sections.text: THE PRIMARY BAND OF WESTERLIES LIES FROM THE PACIFIC NORTHWEST STATES INTO THE CANADIAN PRAIRIES...WITH THE SOUTHERN EXTENT OF MODERATE FLOW EXTENDING FROM WY INTO THE DAKOTAS. MODEL GUIDANCE SUGGESTS STORMS ARE LIKELY TO DEVELOP ALONG THE APPROACHING COLD FRONT OVER MANITOBA AND THE WESTERN DAKOTAS...SPREADING SOUTHEASTWARD INTO MM THROUGH THE EVENING. STRONG INSTABILITY AHEAD OF THE FRONT /DEWPOINTS NEAR 70F AND MLCAPE VALUES OVER 3000 J/KG/ WILL PROMOTE VIGOROUS UPDRAFTS AND A RISK OF LARGE HAIL. FAVORABLE EFFECTIVE SHEAR VALUES ALSO SUGGEST A RISK OF A FEW SUPERCELLS THROUGH THE AFTERNOON/EVENING CAPABLE OF VERY LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS.

sections.title: ME/NH
sections.text: THUNDERSTORMS HAVE COMMENCED DEVELOPING AHEAD OF AN APPROACHING SHORTWAVE TROUGH OVER ONT/QUE. AMPLE MOISTURE/INSTABILITY AND SUFFICIENT DEEP LAYER SHEAR WILL FAVOR SUPERCELL STORM STRUCTURES CAPABLE OF LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS. PLEASE REFERENCE WW 593 AND MCD 1494 FOR FURTHER DETAILS.

sections.title: KY/TN INTO MID ATLANTIC REGION
sections.text: SEVERAL BANDS OF ONGOING THUNDERSTORMS OVER KY/TN WILL LIKELY PERSIST THROUGH THE DAY AND SPREAD INTO PARTS OF VA/NC THIS AFTERNOON. STEEP LOW LEVEL LAPSE RATES AND DEWPOINTS IN THE 70S WILL COMPENSATE FOR RATHER WEAK MID LEVEL WINDS...LEADING TO A RISK OF LOCALLY DAMAGING WINDS IN THE STRONGER CELLS. REFER TO MCD 1495 FOR FURTHER DETAILS.

sections.title: AZ
sections.text: CONSIDERABLE BOUNDARY LAYER MOISTURE IS IN PLACE AGAIN TODAY OVER CENTRAL/SOUTHERN AZ WITH PWAT VALUES NOW RANGING FROM 1.5-1.9 INCHES. BROKEN CLOUDS ARE ERODING...WHICH WILL LEAD TO AFTERNOON MLCAPE VALUES OVER 2000 J/KG. THE STEERING FLOW PATTERN IS SIMILAR TO YESTERDAY...WHICH SHOULD HELP ANY CONVECTION THAT FORMS OVER THE MOUNTAINS OF EASTERN AZ TO SPREAD EAST-NORTHEASTWARD INTO THE LOWER DESERTS. ANY LARGER CLUSTERS OF STORMS THAT FORM WILL POSE A RISK OF LOCALLY GUSTY/DAMAGING WINDS. ..HART/ROGERS.. 07/04/2011

sections.title: 20Z UPDATE
sections.text: ONLY RELATIVELY MINOR CHANGES TO THE PRIOR OUTLOOK HAVE BEEN MADE TO TAKE INTO ACCOUNT ONGOING TRENDS IN DESTABILIZATION AND CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT.

sections.title: CENTRAL/SRN APPALACHIANS INTO MID ATLANTIC COAST
sections.text: THERE STILL APPEARS TO BE POTENTIAL FOR A GROWING/STRENGTHENING SURFACE COLD POOL...WHICH COULD BE ACCOMPANIED BY A BROADER SCALE STRONG/POTENTIALLY DAMAGING WIND THREAT LATE THIS AFTERNOON AND EVENING. STORMS ARE CURRENTLY INCREASING IN COVERAGE AND CONSOLIDATING NEAR AND TO THE EAST OF THE CENTRAL/SOUTHERN APPALACHIANS. AND GUIDANCE SUGGESTS THAT A MID-LEVEL SPEED MAXIMUM /30-35 KT AT 500 MB/ PROPAGATING EAST NORTHEASTWARD OUT OF THE TENNESSEE VALLEY...COULD ENHANCE FORWARD PROPAGATION.

sections.title: OZARK PLATEAU INTO THE TENNESSEE VALLEY AND GULF STATES
sections.text: CONSIDERABLE THUNDERSTORM ACTIVITY IS ALREADY ONGOING...AND LIKELY TO BECOME INCREASINGLY WIDESPREAD THROUGH THE REMAINDER OF THE AFTERNOON IN THE PRESENCE OF STRONG INSTABILITY. HOWEVER... POTENTIAL FOR CONSOLIDATION INTO A SUSTAINED AND AT LEAST SOMEWHAT ORGANIZED MESOSCALE CONVECTIVE SYSTEM STILL APPEARS LOW...AND ANY SEVERE THREAT PROBABLY WILL REMAIN RELATIVELY SPARSE IN COVERAGE AND CONFINED TO GENERALLY STRONGER PULSING STORMS.

sections.title: NORTHERN PLAINS
sections.text: HIGHER END SLIGHT RISK PROBABILITIES HAVE BEEN MAINTAINED AS IS FOR NOW...BUT UNCERTAINTY IS INCREASING CONCERNING STORM COVERAGE LATE THIS AFTERNOON AS INHIBITION REMAINS STRONG...AND SUBSTANTIVE MID-LEVEL FORCING ASSOCIATED WITH THE SASKATCHEWAN/MANITOBA SHORT WAVE TROUGH STAYS NORTH OF THE INTERNATIONAL BORDER. HIGHER STORM COVERAGE COULD END UP ACROSS THE NORTH CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS INTO SOUTH DAKOTA LATER TONIGHT...AS A WEAKER SHORT WAVE IMPULSE EMERGES FROM THE MONSOONAL FLOW REGIME OVER THE INTERMOUNTAIN WEST. ..KERR.. 07/04/2011 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1127 AM CDT MON JUL 04 2011/

sections.title: NRN PLAINS
sections.text: CLUSTER OF STORMS IS MOVING SEWD ACROSS NRN MN ATTM...WITH INCREASING CU FIELD NOTED ALONG THE SURFACE FRONT EXTENDING FROM THIS CONVECTION SWWD ACROSS SERN ND INTO WRN SD -- WHERE A MUCH LARGER CLUSTER OF STORMS IS EVOLVING. AIRMASS ACROSS THIS REGION REMAINS VERY UNSTABLE...AND WITH LARGE-SCALE ASCENT SPREADING EWD TOWARD THIS AREA PER WV IMAGERY COMBINED WITH AN INCREASING SLY LOW-LEVEL JET THIS EVENING...STORM COVERAGE SHOULD CONTINUE TO EXPAND. MODERATE MID-LEVEL WIND FIELD FROM PARTS OF NEB NWD WILL SUPPORT STORM ORGANIZATION...PARTICULARLY GIVEN THE FAVORABLE THERMODYNAMIC ENVIRONMENT. DAMAGING WINDS WILL BE MOST LIKELY WHERE STORMS CAN ORGANIZE/MERGE INTO LINEAR CLUSTERS...WHILE VERY LARGE HAIL WILL ALSO BE POSSIBLE WITH THE STRONGER STORMS -- AS CONVECTION SPREADS EWD/SEWD ACROSS THE N CENTRAL CONUS OVERNIGHT.

sections.title: MID ATLANTIC/CAROLINAS
sections.text: WIDESPREAD STORMS HAVE BEEN ONGOING FROM ROUGHLY THE MASON/DIXON LINE SWD ACROSS THE CAROLINAS OVER THE PAST COUPLE OF HOURS...THOUGH MUCH OF THE MOST FAVORABLY UNSTABLE AIRMASS HAS NOW BEEN CONVECTIVELY OVERTURNED. WHILE ISOLATED STRONGER STORMS/STORM CLUSTERS WILL LIKELY STILL PRODUCE GUSTY WINDS AND HAIL...THREAT HAS DIMINISHED FROM A COUPLE OF HOURS AGO -- AND WILL CONTINUE TO SLOWLY DO SO THE REMAINDER OF THE EVENING. THEREFORE...WILL MAINTAIN ONLY 5% SEVERE PROBABILITIES THIS FORECAST.

sections.title: ARKLATEX EWD INTO THE SOUTHEAST
sections.text: WIDESPREAD STORMS CONTINUE FROM PARTS OF TX/OK EWD ACROSS THE GULF COAST STATES...WHERE WEAK FLOW BUT POCKETS OF MODERATE INSTABILITY EXIST. ISOLATED STRONGER/PULSE CELLS WILL CONTINUE TO PRODUCE LOCALLY GUSTY WINDS AND HAIL ACROSS MUCH OF THIS REGION...BUT AN OVERALL DECREASING TREND WILL BE ONGOING THROUGH THE EVENING.

sections.title: AZ
sections.text: ISOLATED STORMS CONTINUE ACROSS AZ...WITH THE MOST SIGNIFICANT CONVECTION ATTM BEING A SMALL CLUSTER OF CELLS OVER PIMA COUNTY MOVING QUICKLY WWD. LOCALLY DAMAGING GUSTS REMAIN POSSIBLE WITH THIS STORM CLUSTER...AND POSSIBLY WITH A COUPLE OF OTHER ISOLATED/STRONGER CELLS THIS EVENING. HOWEVER...LACK OF CONVECTIVE COVERAGE PRECLUDES ADDITION OF HIGHER SEVERE PROBABILITIES. ..GOSS.. 07/05/2011
